<!--
HOW TO USE THIS FILE (the manual is workflow/03-manuscript.md)
- Replace every [FILL: ...] and delete the HTML comments that instruct you. Chunks marked eval: false
  are patterns to copy; remove that line once a chunk is real.
- Every number in the text comes through prov(), from results/. Never type a result.
- Markers are spans: [TO CONFIRM: the decision]{.tc} for anything a person must decide,
  [CITE: the claim]{.cite} for a claim without a usable source.
- Write in this order: purpose draft of the Introduction; the design proposal (stop); the quick run;
  Methods, Design, Results, Discussion; Introduction revised; Abstract.
- No workflow words in the paper (pilot, card, worker, quick run, spec, harness, known-answer check, the report).
- The proofs go in _supplement.qmd, included after the references as the supplementary note.
- Render: quarto render manuscript.qmd            (draft mode, with the banner and gap table)
          quarto render manuscript.qmd -P draft:false   (final mode, when production numbers exist)
- Check:  python3 -I check-manuscript.py manuscript.qmd manuscript.html --citations citations.csv --bib references.bib --journals ../workflow/journals/journals.csv --journal <slug>
-->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

source("manuscript-helpers.R")
prov_set_mode(params$draft)
ri <- read_run_info()   # results/run_info.rds, written by the analysis scripts
if (!params$draft) check_no_markers("manuscript.qmd")

# [FILL] Load every results file here and compute every quoted number from these objects.
# reps <- read_results("simulation_replicates.rds")
# design <- read_results("design.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: draft-banner
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr params$draft

cat(draft_banner(qmd = "manuscript.qmd"))
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

<!-- The headings and word limit of the target journal's profile (journals/profiles/<slug>.md).
BMC Bioinformatics: Background, Results, Conclusions, 350 words. PLOS ONE: unstructured, 300 words.
Every claim carries a numeric result with its uncertainty, through prov(): an estimate with its
confidence interval or Monte Carlo SE, a rate with its band, a count against its permutation count.
Quick-run numbers in the first draft. Write it last. -->

# Introduction

<!-- Paragraph 1: open with why (the scientific question the procedure serves and what a user hopes to
learn from it), then the procedure people use, where and how it is used, and what its output is taken
to estimate, ending with one concrete published example: the data, what was computed, and how its
authors read the estimate. Paragraph 2: the realistic condition; what the procedure estimates under it, in words and
then as a formula; what has been observed or derived before, saying for each source what it did and
did not do, and ending with what has not been derived. Paragraph 3: what this paper does, in the
order of the sections. Almost every sentence is a fact with a reference; the rest build the tension
and resolve it. Plain language before the formal statement. The claims are the aims, as questions. -->
